q: Why won’t Basic PAYE Tools open on my Mac?
a: Since macOS Sequoia, the part of Basic PAYE Tools that runs in the background no longer starts by itself. HMRC acknowledge the problem on macOS 15 Sequoia, 26 Tahoe and 27 Golden Gate, and their workaround uses the Terminal app every time you run payroll. PayrollRTI does those steps for you, so Basic PAYE Tools opens with a double-click.

q: Does Basic PAYE Tools work on macOS 27 Golden Gate?
a: Not on its own. On macOS 27 Golden Gate, as on 26 Tahoe and 15 Sequoia, HMRC’s Basic PAYE Tools won’t open without their Terminal workaround. With PayrollRTI it opens with a double-click. macOS 27 only runs on Apple silicon Macs, where PayrollRTI can run HMRC’s Mac app through Rosetta, or HMRC’s Linux version with no Rosetta at all.

q: Basic PAYE Tools is stuck on “Starting application”. What can I do?
a: That is the same problem: the part of Basic PAYE Tools that runs in the background hasn’t started, so the window waits for it forever. Quit Basic PAYE Tools, install PayrollRTI, and open Basic PAYE Tools through PayrollRTI instead. Your payroll data stays where it is.

q: Will Basic PAYE Tools still work on macOS 28, when Rosetta is removed?
a: HMRC’s Mac app is built for Intel Macs, so on an Apple silicon Mac it only runs through Rosetta. Apple say macOS 27 Golden Gate is the last version with full Rosetta, and from macOS 28 only some older games will keep it. PayrollRTI can run HMRC’s Linux version of Basic PAYE Tools instead, which needs no Rosetta, so it is built to keep working on macOS 28 and later.

q: Do I need Rosetta to run Basic PAYE Tools?
a: On an Apple silicon Mac, HMRC’s Mac app needs Rosetta, and PayrollRTI can install it for you while Apple still offer it. HMRC’s Linux version, run by PayrollRTI, does not need Rosetta at all. Intel Macs never need Rosetta.

q: What is the Linux version, and is it the same Basic PAYE Tools?
a: HMRC publish Basic PAYE Tools for Windows, Mac and Linux on GOV.UK. Inside, the Linux version is the same program as the Mac app, packaged differently. PayrollRTI downloads it from GOV.UK and runs it on a small runtime built for Apple silicon. HMRC’s files are not changed, and PayrollRTI does not copy or redistribute them. You get the same screens, the same calculations and the same submissions to HMRC.

q: Has the Linux version been tested with real payroll?
a: Yes. Real backups were restored into it, P60s were produced, and live submissions to HMRC (a NINO verification request and a Full Payment Submission) were accepted. A month’s pay run entered in both HMRC’s Mac app and the Linux version produced identical submissions. Back up before you switch, as you would before any update.

Everything runs on your own Mac, and PayrollRTI does not send your data anywhere. Both ways of running Basic PAYE Tools use the same payroll data in your HMRC folder. PayrollRTI backs it up before it downloads the Linux version and before any update that changes your data. Read looking after your payroll data before you switch.

q: Can I switch back to HMRC’s Mac app?
a: Yes, in PayrollRTI’s Settings, as long as both are the same version of Basic PAYE Tools. A newer version updates your payroll data when it first starts, and older versions cannot open it after that. So if the Linux version updates to a new release, install the same release of HMRC’s Mac app from GOV.UK before you switch back.

q: I already use PayrollRTI. How do I update?
a: Download the latest version and drag it to Applications, choosing Replace. Your payroll data stays where it is. From version 0.2.0, PayrollRTI checks for new versions and updates itself.

a: macOS 15 Sequoia and later, including 26 Tahoe and 27 Golden Gate (macOS was called OS X until 2016). The Linux version needs an Apple silicon Mac (M1 or later). Intel Macs keep using HMRC’s Mac app, which runs on them without Rosetta. To check your Mac, open the Apple menu and choose About This Mac.
